messages.body_plain:
Hi!

Arguably, that is an instance of bad style in the code, but I wonder why it causes an error with your compiler. (In essence, the compiler seems to think there is some way to end the function without "returning" a value. But clearly, there is not. Which compiler/version is this?).

Anyway, you can probably help your compiler along by replacing the file rkward/plugin/rkcomponent.cpp with this version, here: https://sourceforge.net/p/rkward/code/HEAD/tree/trunk/rkward/rkward/plugin/rkcomponent.cpp?format=raw

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Hi!

> index.docbook:11: warning: failed to load external entity "dtd/kdex.dtd"

For some reason, the main docbook declaration can't be found. I _guess_ this problem may be due to trying to install to a local path, which is not well tested. As a very quick and dirty workaround, edit CMakeLists.txt in the top source directory, and remove the line

> ADD_SUBDIRECTORY(doc)

Most parts of the documentation will still be available (as it does not rely on KDE's help system), and the "writing plugins" documentation is also available online (<http://rkward.sourceforge.net/documents/devel/plugins/index.html>)

But just to make sure: You are aware that a) binaries are available for Ubuntu (<https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel/+archive/rkward-stable-cran> is the one you'll need for RKWard 0.6.1 and R >= 3.0.0), and b) you can also use this to build from source (apt-get build)?

Using .debs has the advantage that you can install to the system path (which is much more reliable for many KDE apps), and still be able to remove the software, cleanly, if needed.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] rkward script editor popups
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

On Tuesday 24 June 2014 17:45:13 Paul Zerr wrote:
> I love the program so far, really great, thank you, developers!

Thanks. We like to hear that!
 
> One thing is really annoying and I can't find a way to turn it off:
> anywhere I click in the script editor a blue popup opens that seems to
> provide information about the libraries in use.

Hm, either there is a bit of exaggeration in that "anywhere", or it is a bug. 
Two types of popups are to be expected inside the script editor: code 
completion and function argument hinting. You can these turn off, separately, 
at Settings->Configure RKWard->Script Editor.

>From your description, it sounds like it's something entirely different, 
though, which really does not belong there. Please provide:

a) The output of rk.sessionInfo()
b) A small screenshot or text copy of the content of the popup.
c) Could it be this is the tooltip from the workspace browser, somehow? Click 
on the "Workspace" tool button to toggle the workspace browser on or off. See 
if that affects anything.

Regards
Thomas
